content: When a long-running process (e.g., PM2) is started before a new function is added to the codebase, subsequent evolution cycles will silently run the old code without the new function, producing no output and no errors. Always verify that the running process version matches the deployed code version by checking logs for expected log messages (e.g., 'Evolution knowledge recorded') and using process restart mechanisms when code updates are detected.
summary: Ensure running process version matches deployed code; restart after code updates.
rationale: Evolution #031 identified that PM2 was started before recordEvolutionKnowledge was added, causing cycles #2-#7 to silently run old code with no knowledge files produced. The fix required a process restart, which the agent triggered via requestRestart.

content: When a trigger threshold uses a hard-coded confidence cutoff (e.g., `confidence > 0.7`) but the recommended action always produces a lower confidence score (e.g., 0.6 for 'balanced'), the system will permanently remain in a suboptimal state regardless of real-world conditions. Audit all numeric thresholds against the actual output ranges of the functions that feed them, and lower the threshold (e.g., from 0.7 to 0.5) or raise the emitted confidence to match.
summary: Audit numeric thresholds against the actual confidence ranges that feed them.
rationale: Evolution #037 fixed getCurrentStrategy() whose 0.7 cutoff blocked the 'balanced' recommendation (confidence=0.6), permanently locking the system in 'repair-only' mode even at 0% failure rate.

content: When adding a trigger condition that requires a minimum history count (e.g., MIN_HISTORY_FOR_REFLECTION=3), always provide a time-based fallback (e.g., every 6 hours) so that advanced self-improvement subsystems are not silently skipped when history data is lost or sparse. Additionally, ensure that every subsystem intended for the main loop is actually called in that loop, not just imported in unrelated modules.
summary: Pair minimum-history triggers with time-based fallbacks to avoid silent skipping.
rationale: Evolution #032 found that shouldTriggerReflection required 3 history records (only 1 existed) and that the metacognitive system was never called from the main loop at all, meaning both self-improvement systems had never executed.

content: When a test file imports from a relative path that does not match the compiled output directory (e.g., `./failure-patterns.js` instead of `../dist/memory/failure-patterns.js`), the test suite silently skips the entire file. Always verify that test import paths resolve to the actual compiled artifact location (`dist/`) and fix them immediately so coverage is not lost.
summary: Test import paths must resolve to compiled dist/ artifacts, not source-relative stubs.
rationale: Evolution #043 found that failure-patterns.test.ts imported from './failure-patterns.js' which did not exist; fixing the path to '../dist/memory/failure-patterns.js' restored 25 previously invisible tests.

content: When implementing a feature (e.g., a new command or module) that references a function name in a shorthand property initializer, verify that the declared variable name exactly matches the function name before committing. A mismatch (e.g., using `capabilitySummary` as shorthand when only `capabilitySection` is defined) causes a silent TypeScript error that passes tests but breaks runtime behavior.
summary: Verify shorthand property names match declared function names to avoid silent TypeScript errors.
rationale: Evolution #038 introduced a TypeScript error by using `capabilitySummary` as a shorthand property while the actual function was named `capabilitySection`, caught only during the pre-commit build step.

content: When a module uses symbols from a namespace import (e.g., `fs.existsSync`, `path.join`) in one code region but those imports are absent, and a different region uses named imports of the same utilities (e.g., `existsSync`, `join`), the TypeScript compiler will report 'Cannot find name' errors that tests may not catch. Audit all symbol usages against the import list at review time and replace namespace-style calls with the already-imported named bindings.
summary: Replace namespace-style fs/path calls with already-imported named bindings to fix TS errors.
rationale: Evolution #053 found that archive-integration.ts used `fs.existsSync` and `path.join` without importing them, while `existsSync` and `join` were already imported as named bindings, causing TypeScript compilation errors undetected by the test suite.

content: Implement span-based tracing in every long-running agent loop by wrapping each logical phase (understand, implement, commit) in a named span with start time, end time, and success/error status. Without per-phase spans, it is impossible to pinpoint which phase failed or was slow, and retrospective self-improvement signals are unreliable. Store spans to a persistent file so post-hoc analysis can reconstruct the full execution chain.
summary: Wrap each agent loop phase in a named span with timestamps and status for full traceability.
rationale: Evolution #045 (Arize research) and #054 (tracing integration) established that without span-based tracing there is no ground-truth record of which phase of each evolution cycle succeeded or failed, making diagnosis guesswork.

content: Design self-improvement systems as a closed feedback loop: (1) distill abstract, reusable principles from past interaction trajectories offline; (2) retrieve the most relevant principles before each new decision; (3) record whether applying each principle led to success or failure; and (4) prune or update principles based on observed success rates. Without this loop, each decision is made from scratch and the system cannot accumulate structured operational knowledge.
summary: Build a trajectory→principle→retrieval→feedback loop for structured knowledge accumulation.
rationale: Evolutions #047, #049, #050, #052 implemented the EvolveR two-stage distillation architecture: principle-distiller.ts extracts principles from history, principle-retriever.ts injects them into the evolution prompt, completing the feedback loop.

content: Adopt a structured evolution asset protocol (analogous to GEP Genes/Capsules/Events) to transform ad-hoc prompt decisions into auditable, reusable assets. Each evolution task should emit: (a) a Gene-like strategy object capturing the signal pattern and execution steps used, (b) a Capsule-like record when a strategy succeeds (with environment fingerprint and blast radius), and (c) an append-only Event log entry. This enables signal-driven strategy selection instead of LLM re-reasoning from scratch on every cycle.
summary: Emit structured Gene/Capsule/Event assets per evolution to enable signal-driven strategy reuse.
rationale: Evolution #046 analyzed the EvoMap/evolver GEP protocol and identified that Jinx re-reasons strategy from scratch each cycle, whereas GEP's signal-matched Genes and solidified Capsules allow direct reuse of successful patterns without repeated LLM inference.

content: Maintain an Agent Archive of parallel evolution branches to avoid converging prematurely to a local optimum. Each branch should track fitness score, diversity score, and exploration tags. Use a balanced selection strategy (e.g., 60% fitness weight, 40% diversity weight) when choosing which branch to continue. Automatically spawn a new exploration branch when overall diversity drops below a threshold (e.g., 0.15) or all active branches are stagnant.
summary: Keep a multi-branch agent archive with diversity scoring to escape local optima.
rationale: Evolution #053 studied the Darwin Gödel Machine and found that single-path evolution (Jinx's prior approach) is prone to local optima; the archive mechanism with diversity metrics is the key innovation that lifted SWE-bench performance from 20% to 50%.

content: When integrating an external API (e.g., Exa Search), add explicit debug logging that records the full request body and the raw response before parsing. When a 'required field missing' error occurs despite the field being present in your payload, test adding undocumented required parameters (e.g., `useApiKey: true`) and verify the fix against the provider's latest documentation, since API contracts can change without a version bump.
summary: Log full API request/response bodies and test undocumented parameters when 'required field' errors occur.
rationale: Evolution #051 fixed an Exa API 'Required at query' error by adding `useApiKey: true` to the request body; the existing fallback chain (Brave → Serper) was already in place, demonstrating defense-in-depth for external search integrations.

content: When designing a Telegram bot command that performs multi-step data retrieval and formatting, extract each logical concern (argument parsing, data retrieval, result formatting, age calculation) into named helper functions defined outside the command handler closure. Command handler closures exceeding approximately 100 lines or cyclomatic complexity 15 will typically fail ESLint rules and reduce maintainability; splitting them also makes unit testing each step independently feasible.
summary: Extract Telegram command logic into small named helpers to stay under ESLint complexity limits.
rationale: Evolution #042 implemented /recall and hit ESLint cyclomatic-complexity (27 > 15) and line-count (145 > 100) violations, requiring a full refactor of the command handler into smaller helpers before the commit could succeed.

content: When the pre-commit hook fails due to pre-existing ESLint or TypeScript errors that are unrelated to the current change, use `git commit --no-verify` only as a documented, last-resort escape hatch for documentation-only or research-only commits. For any code change, fix all lint errors introduced by that change before committing, and track pre-existing errors as separate backlog items so they are not silently accumulated.
summary: Use --no-verify only for doc-only commits; fix all lint errors introduced by code changes before committing.
rationale: Multiple evolutions (#033, #035, #036, #043, #049, #051, #053) used --no-verify to bypass pre-commit hooks due to pre-existing lint errors, creating a pattern of accumulated technical debt that blocks normal commits and hides regressions.

content: When evaluating whether to add MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool support to an agent framework that explicitly forbids MCP at its core (e.g., Pi's 'No MCP' design), implement tool-scope control as an extension using environment variables (e.g., JINX_TOOL_GROUPS) to activate only needed tool subsets. This mirrors the X-MCP-Tools header pattern for reducing context window usage without modifying the core framework.
summary: Implement tool-group filtering via env vars as an extension rather than modifying the core framework.
rationale: Evolution #044 evaluated GitHub MCP's X-MCP-Tools header for per-tool configuration and implemented an analogous ToolGroupManager in Jinx's extension layer, achieving context reduction without violating the Pi framework's No-MCP constraint.

content: Apply the SICA self-modification safety pattern: before any self-directed code change, explicitly estimate the blast radius (files affected, lines changed), define validation commands that must pass after the change, and enforce a rollback policy if validation fails. Never skip validation on self-modifications, as failed self-edits that are not rolled back can corrupt the agent's own execution environment.
summary: Estimate blast radius and enforce validation+rollback before every self-directed code modification.
rationale: Evolution #036 studied SICA (Self-Improving Coding Agent) and identified its core safety mechanism as the combination of pre-change impact estimation, post-change validation, and automatic rollback—absent in Jinx's current loop, where self-edits are not explicitly bounded.
